### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_
- `content/docs/capabilities/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 48 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d520e11bb833ef76b851b765bfc663b0309c7359` — the merge of head `060935978a865d64bdde9841dd7f644526e08a7d` into base `64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d520e11bb833ef76b851b765bfc663b0309c7359 && git checkout d520e11bb833ef76b851b765bfc663b0309c7359
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df 060935978a865d64bdde9841dd7f644526e08a7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df && git merge --no-ff 060935978a865d64bdde9841dd7f644526e08a7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 64646aed2ef5ebb2c628c50d9f3fab19a43c62df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `060935978a865d64bdde9841dd7f644526e08a7d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-head-manager-reads.test.ts — the PR also declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the narrowing floor applies and every non-prose path of the diff is in scope; the only remainder is the prose face, `.changeset/29792-team-manager-read-refuses.md`, judged in ② only. Cited code read, not reviewed: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts`, `sharing-rule-service.ts`, `ownership-queue-service.ts`, `position-graph.ts`, `manager-org-screen.test.ts`, `sharing-rule.test.ts`; `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` (`lookupManager`); `packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts`, `object-absence.ts`; `packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts` and `packages/spec/package.json` (`exports`); `docs/adr/0057` D3; the predecessor `a5650194` (#29787) and the JSDoc-only spec precedent `f125ce40da` (#29238). hotcrm `origin/main` `d4ffe99` and docs.objectos.ai `origin/main` `4678114` grepped for every symbol named below.

Inputs: card #29792 (body, triage 6596322022, claim 6596391821, os-dev-report 6597412637), PR #29836 body, file list and net diff against `main` (5 files from merge-base `b0ef25f524`; `pr.diff` matches `git diff b0ef25f524 pr29836 --name-only` exactly), and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`TeamGraphService.managerOf` (team-graph.ts, on the package index) narrows: a failed `sys_user` read throws instead of answering `null`.** Right. The `try { engine.find } catch { row = null }` is replaced by `readMembershipToCompletion(..., { object: 'sys_user', where: { id: userId }, fields: ['manager_id'], subject, kind: 'lookup' })`. In the walk, a non-absence error reaches `throw holderReadRefusal(subject, message, err, 'lookup')`, which `Object.assign`s the driver error as `cause`. The message is `[sharing] the manager of user 'ID' could not be read: REASON. Answering "none" would drop the person it names from everything routed through the answer, so the lookup refuses instead.` The pin asserts the `cause.code` is the driver's `SQLITE_IOERR`.
2. **Nothing is cached after a failed read.** Right. The throw happens inside `readMembershipToCompletion`, before `this.cache.manager!.set(key, mgr)`; the next call on the same instance misses the cache and reads again (pinned: fail once, then `usr_bob`). The cache key is unchanged: `${org ?? '*'}::${userId}` with `org = organizationId ?? this.organizationId`, the #10231 composite key; the `has`/`get ?? null` read before the lookup is unchanged.
3. **Absence still answers `null`, and that `null` is cached.** Right. `isObjectAbsentError(err, 'sys_user')` (OBJECT_NOT_FOUND naming `sys_user`, or the driver's missing-table refusal for it) returns `null` from the walk, `rows?.[0]` is `undefined`, `mgr` is `null`, cached. Caching absence is the #29787 `headOf` shape too: absence IS an answer. Pinned twice (object never registered; table dropped on a real SQLite driver).
4. **`managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg` unchanged.** Right, byte-identical between `origin/main` and the head (diffed the function body). Its `catch { return false }` on `sys_member` stays the #10153 fail-open; the new control pin fails only `sys_member` and asserts the manager is kept. Observation, not a finding: the kept manager is cached for the pass as before — the ruled posture, unchanged here.
5. **S4, `holderReadRefusal` gains a `lookup` arm; `expansion` and `check` sentences unchanged.** Right. The two existing strings are byte-identical in the diff (only the ternary nests one level). `HolderReadKind = 'expansion' | 'check' | 'lookup'` is a module-local type; `readMembershipToCompletion`'s `kind?` widens to it. That function and `probeMembership` are not on `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts` (unchanged, grepped at the head), and the package's `exports` map is `.` only, so the widened parameter is not a published surface: no `Clause-②: yes` is owed for it. `BusinessUnitGraphService.headOf` and the standalone `managerOf` now pass `kind: 'lookup'`; their subjects (`the head of business unit 'ID'`, `the manager of user 'ID'`) are unchanged, so every existing pin that matches the first clause still matches.
6. **The wired `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` limb now passes a refusal through.** Right, by construction: `if (this.teamGraph) return this.teamGraph.managerOf(userId, organizationId)` is unchanged; only the JSDoc gained the #29792 sentence. Both limbs now refuse with the same subject and reason, which is what the reshaped CONTROL pin asserts.
7. **`expandPrincipal` (on the package index) `manager` arm now refuses.** Right. The function body is byte-identical to `main`; `const mgr = await ctx.team.managerOf(...)` has no catch, so the refusal propagates where `[]` used to come back. Pinned both ways (`[usr_bob]` healthy; rejects on a failed read).
8. **S3.** Right. The `[#29713] CONTROL` pin drops both `toBeNull()` lines; the equality control is kept as `settled(wired) toEqual settled(team)` on the failed read, plus the unchanged healthy equality. `settled` reduces a refusal to `{ refused: message }`, so the control compares the refusal text of the two limbs, which is identical (same subject, same driver reason).
9. **S1, `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`.** Prose only: two `/** */` blocks on `ITeamGraphService.managerOf` and `IBusinessUnitGraphService.headOf`; no signature, key, type or export changes (verified against `main` lines 662-690). The file is published: `packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts` does `export * from './sharing-service.js'` and `package.json` `exports['./contracts']` points at `dist/contracts/index.d.ts`/`.d.mts`, so the JSDoc ships. `check:api-surface` indexes names, not comments, so it is unaffected (and Spec property liveness passed on the head).
10. **Callers (the card's STOP condition), traced myself.** No caller fails a whole pass where it dropped one person:
    - objectstack `origin/main` (`64646aed2e`): `expandPrincipal` has no non-test caller anywhere (only `sharing-rule.test.ts`, which does not fail reads). `SharingRuleService` builds a `TeamGraphService` and calls only `team.expandUsers` (line 2119); `ownership-queue-service.ts` only `team.expandUsers` (332); `PositionGraphService` only `teamGraph.expandRoleUsers` (119); `plugin-approvals` resolves managers through its own `lookupManager` (approval-service.ts 2637, 3595) and never imports `TeamGraphService`. `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` has no production caller (the #29787 trace, re-grepped). `plugin-auth/admin-set-user-manager.ts` and `plugin-approvals/manager-org-screen-parity.contract.test.ts` name `TeamGraphService.managerOf` in comments only. The only other implementers of the two interfaces are the two classes in this package; hotcrm and docs.objectos.ai have none.
    - hotcrm `origin/main` `d4ffe99`: pins `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` 18.2.0 but references none of `managerOf`, `expandPrincipal`, `TeamGraphService`, `BusinessUnitGraphService`, `ITeamGraphService`, `IBusinessUnitGraphService` (the one `managerOf` hit is a local variable in `test/hierarchy-read-depth.test.ts`).
    - docs.objectos.ai `origin/main` `4678114`: no reference.
11. **No change to `protocol.ts`, metadata, the package index, or any generated spec artifact.** Right (5-file diff; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset` green).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29792-team-manager-read-refuses.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`; both line-initial declarations present and matching the PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; title carries `!`; a `**BREAKING** only where the read fails` banner; one adr-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the same form as #29787's. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, a non-protocol narrowing "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition", and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. Right.
- `@objectstack/spec` patch for JSDoc that ships in `dist/contracts/index.d.ts`: right. The change publishes new comment bytes in a released package, so it is not `skip-changeset`; it changes no type, so `minor` is not owed; the repo's precedent `f125ce40da` (#29238, JSDoc-only on `automation-service.ts`) took exactly a spec `patch`. Triage 6596322022 ruled the JSDoc rides in this one `domain:server` PR.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm: nothing is added to the published accept set; one published behaviour narrows (`null` on a failed read becomes a throw) on `TeamGraphService.managerOf`, `expandPrincipal`'s `manager` arm and the wired `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf`. The `readMembershipToCompletion` `kind` widening is off the `exports` map (① item 5), so it is not a `yes`.
- Every changeset sentence checked against the tree: "the holder reads of `TeamGraphService`, and the head and standalone manager lookups of `BusinessUnitGraphService`, already refuse" (true since #29503/#29362/#29787); "nothing is cached after a failed read" (① 2); "`BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` when it is built with a `teamGraph`" (① 6); "judged by `isObjectAbsentError`" (① 3); "the organization screen is unchanged" (① 4); "a failed head or manager lookup now says it is a lookup of one person" (① 5); the JSDoc quote matches the file verbatim; "no sharing rule, approval or ownership queue on this release calls `managerOf` or `expandPrincipal`" (① 10). Consistent.
- Check-runs on `0609359` at this record's third read: 61 runs, 22 success (among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate), 9 skipped (opt-in and UI-only families), 30 still in progress: Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core 1-8, Type Check UI, Test UI 1-16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. No failure at any read. The outstanding conclusions are the landing-time "all green" condition, which the dispatching seat reads at landing; this record does not stand in for them, and a red among them on this head would need a delta record.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.
- `open_questions`: `[]`. None to answer.
- `Skills-docs: not needed`: verified. No skill, `.claude/**`, `content/docs/**` or `apps/docs/**` page names `TeamGraphService.managerOf`, `expandPrincipal` or `holderReadRefusal`. The one ADR hit, ADR-0057 D3, cites the `managerOf` chain for bounding and org-scoping only, not for its failure answer; nothing there contradicts a refusal.
- Dev deviation "the relay refused an empty labels array, so the PR carries none": the head now carries `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling` from Auto Label; nothing owed to the tree.
- Dev deviation "three scratch gate files written to the container root": outside the repo; the net diff is the 5 declared files, so none of them rides.
- Dev's cross-repo trace cites docs.objectos.ai at `4a00661`; that object does not exist in this container's clone, whose `origin/main` is `4678114`. My trace at `4678114` finds no reference either, so the STOP conclusion stands; the PR body's sha is a provenance nit, not a finding (not a `hits` file).
- Measurement provenance: the PR's "measured first" table and ablations are the dev's own account; not relied on here. Every judgment above is from the tree and the pins as written.
- Escalations: none.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` (hits, schema face, judged against the ruling it implements and its implementers).** The two JSDoc sentences now say "refuses (throws) on a failed read; `null` when none". Against the only implementers: `TeamGraphService.managerOf` at the head throws on a failed read, answers `null` for no `manager_id`, a screened-out cross-org manager, an unknown user, an empty `userId`, or an absent `sys_user` — every one of those is "none" in the contract's sense (no manager on file for that user in that organization). `BusinessUnitGraphService.headOf` has had the same shape since #29787. The sentence states what the code does now and nothing the code does not do. Attempts to break it: (a) could an implementer read "refuses on a failed read" as obliging it to refuse on absence? No — "`null` when none" is the explicit other branch, and the family's distinction (absence is an answer, `isObjectAbsentError`) lives in the implementations, where it belongs; (b) does the unchanged `IBusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` doc ("proxy to `ITeamGraphService.managerOf`") now mislead? No — both limbs answer the same thing on every path, which is exactly what the reshaped CONTROL pin asserts; (c) the first consumer: none exists on any of the three repositories today, and the first one that names "the owner's manager" gets the posture the three predecessor PRs gave every other grant-deciding read. Holds. No finding.

**Narrowing face, `team-graph.ts`, `business-unit-graph.ts`, `business-unit-head-manager-reads.test.ts` (judged against the published spec on `main`).** Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at a consumer? The published `main` JSDoc promised "best-effort; null when none", which is the swallow being retired; no consumer in objectstack, hotcrm or docs.objectos.ai relied on `null`-on-failure (① 10), and a caller of the exported class or function on a failing driver now gets a `cause`-bearing refusal where it got a cached, wrong "no manager". Does it make the spec's own refusal real? Yes: it is the last read of the family named in the card, and the refusal travels through the one walk and the one refusal sentence family (`readMembershipToCompletion`, `holderReadRefusal`) the rest of the family uses, with no local helper. Attempts to break it: (a) `keysetWalk` on `where: { id: userId }` yields at most one row, far short of the 10,000-row page, so the cursor and `truncated` branches cannot fire for a lookup; the fake engines in `manager-org-screen.test.ts` (which throws on `$`-combinators) and `sharing-rule.test.ts` only ever see the first page's flat equality `where`, so those suites are untouched by the walk; (b) the lookup reads `fields: ['id', 'manager_id']` as before (the walk prepends `id`); (c) the fail-once pin proves the cache `set` is not reached on a refusal, and the fail-open control proves `sys_member` is still swallowed; (d) the refusal's `lookup` sentence names the consequence correctly for a single-person answer and leaves the two older sentences byte-identical. Holds. No finding.

**Nits (not findings, not in the hits files):** the `expandPrincipal` JSDoc on `main` still says "used by the sharing-rule evaluator + approval engine", which neither does; pre-existing, untouched by this diff, a candidate for a follow-up prose card, not for this PR.
